class1003.description: A short, high-energy session to activate airport, hotel, and restaurant vocabulary before your trip.
outcomes: Ask for a room and clarify details
Use polite requests at the airport
React naturally when you do not understand
materialDescriptions: The 24 phrases we will use in class.
Five minutes of announcements and directions.
class1003.teacherNote: Bring one real trip scenario you want to rehearse. We will use it as the final role-play.

class1004.description: Practice introducing yourself, your role, and your company in a professional setting.
outcomes: Open a meeting and hand over the floor
Use follow-up questions that sound natural
materialDescriptions: The lesson that supports today’s class.
Twelve words to review after class.
class1004.teacherNote: Your class is in progress. The room stays open for a few minutes after the start.

class1001.description: A relaxed conversation class built around your week, with corrections only where they matter.
agenda: Set a goal for the next class
outcomes: Tell a short story in the past tense
Use connectors to sound more natural
materialDescriptions: The lesson connected to this class.
A quick drill before we meet.
class1001.teacherNote: We will spend the first five minutes on your week, then move into the past tense story.

class1002.description: A structured review of the past tense with short exercises and a guided conversation.
agenda: Check homework from the last class
outcomes: Choose the right past tense form
Fix the three mistakes you repeat most
Retell a short story without notes
materialDescriptions: One page with the patterns that matter.
class1002.homework: Write five sentences about last weekend and mark the verbs you had to think about.

class0901.description: A completed class on restaurant vocabulary, polite requests, and handling surprises on the menu.
materialDescriptions: Review the words from this class.
class0901.teacherNote: You improved a lot with polite requests. Keep practicing the difference between pedir and preguntar.
class0901.homework: Record a 60-second restaurant order and listen back once.
class0901.recap: You handled the ordering role-play without switching to English. Keep the polite request frames active and rehearse the wrong-order fix once before the next class.

class0902.description: A focused class on vowels, rhythm, and the sounds that make Spanish feel fast.
materialDescriptions: The sounds and drills from class.
class0902.teacherNote: Your rhythm is much better. Keep the shadowing routine for five minutes before each class.
class0902.homework: Shadow the same dialogue three times this week.
class0902.recap: Vowels are cleaner and the rhythm is steadier. The next step is keeping the same pace when you improvise instead of reading.
